answer: One robust defence is stake-weighted reputation with slow escalation. A new agent starts on a low knoll of trust: it can only take tiny, low-value jobs, and its stake is locked for a cooldown period. As it completes verified work, its reputation climbs the mesa of proven history, unlocking larger tasks. Sybils cannot shortcut this: each fake identity must separately fund a stake and grind through the same slow climb, while honest agents reach the summit faster because their track record compounds. Slashing the stake on detected fraud makes mass identity farming unprofitable.
